purpose: Pin which PowerShell command forms invoke a file, so the frontend's native domain for a command is checked against a measurement rather than against a reading of the specification.
note: PowerShell resolves a command name carrying a path separator as a path and anything else through its command table, so `./build.ps1`, `.\build.ps1` and `& './build.ps1'` are one invocation and a bare `build.ps1` reaches no file. A case marked modelled is one the frontend lowers to an Exec. The harness writes the command into a wrapper script and runs `pwsh -File`, because `pwsh -Command` reports 0 or 1 and not the status the script left — which is itself why a workflow's pwsh step carries `exit $LASTEXITCODE`.
subject:
param()
Write-Output "args=$($args -join ',')"
exit 7
